notes: The main round-trips and Pretty() work, but wrappers carry literal-only source ranges and the shallow constant helpers miss validation cases involving nested unary signs.
The String() fix and preservation of literal validation are sound, but Pretty() was not updated and now exposes the synthetic unary plus as '(+5)' or '(+5m)'.
Fixes the round-trips, but inventing an Op == 0 identity expression unnecessarily expands AST, evaluator, printer, and API semantics instead of reusing the supported unary-plus representation.

Preserves the reported forms using existing AST semantics with strong parser, printer, Pretty, and evaluation coverage, although parenthesized zero divisors now bypass the existing division/modulo-by-zero parse checks.

Basic partial returns work, but invoked templates discard return values, bare-return success depends on the execution entry point, and untracked parser and executor modifications undermine fork maintainability.

Common early-return cases work, but shared-context return values can leak from nested executions, commands after return are silently skipped, and executor edits are missing from the fork regeneration script.

Basic early exits work and fork regeneration is addressed, but invoked-template return values are swallowed, pipelines can silently skip commands, and the edited documentation retains contradictory restrictions.

The sentinel supports common early returns, but invoked templates silently discard valued returns, context-based capture adds complexity, and the executor changes are not preserved by fork regeneration.
The implementation covers the primary parser and formatter behavior well, but omits the quoted address-suffix guard and duplicates structural-brace checks instead of centralizing them.
Correctly makes quoted exact braces non-structural across the main parser paths, but misses the quoted address-suffix guard and leaves structural-token comments stale.
It fixes the common parsing paths, but leaves both the quoted address-suffix check and doImport's raw anonymous-block check able to misclassify quoted braces.
The centralized token helpers give good coverage of the main behavior, but the quoted address-suffix case and updated argument documentation are missing.

It matches the expansion-time first-wins design and has strong coverage, though its pre-deduplication compares only resource keys and can mishandle statically addressed resources in for_each module instances.
It fixes multiple root-module imports but still discards every child-module statement for a resource once any ancestor statement exists, even when the instance keys differ.
It correctly preserves static per-instance imports, but its conservative dynamic-key rule can discard child imports for instances not covered by the ancestor block.
It handles static per-instance precedence and the direct regression, but its find-time fallback treats any dynamic address as a whole-resource conflict and drops valid child instances.
It covers the main run path well, but misses lower-layer shortcut handling and execution-segment conflicts while adding unrelated global proxy-environment test changes.
The implementation is readable and well tested for direct execution, but it does not protect scenarios from lower-layer shortcut merging or discard execution-segment settings.
This closely matches the reference, including lower-layer shortcut removal and all relevant conflicts, but the added test helper named onceScenario conflicts with the production helper as shown.
The core transformation works, but applying it only after consolidation leaves lower-layer shortcut replacement possible and omits execution-segment conflicts and cleanup.
It most closely mirrors the reference behavior, handling nested branch paths and resources with focused tests, with only a minor unnecessary cmp-based fallback.
Its slugBaseDir logic closely matches the intended branch and descendant path transformation with good multilingual taxonomy coverage, although the tests do not exercise resources or explicit URLs.

It is a functional, well-tested solution including descendants, resources, and custom URLs, though the concrete CurrentSection assertion and unconditional directory override make it somewhat less robust.

It correctly covers localized section and taxonomy/term paths and descendants, but the SectionBase prefix-rewrite approach is less robust than computing one canonical directory and its tests omit resource and explicit-URL cases.
